paragraphs.text: Abstract. A Ti-6Al-4V lattice structure was fabricated by selective laser melting with a laser power of 170 W and a scan speed of 1100 mm/s, yielding a relative density of 99.2 percent.
Quasi-static compression tests were performed at room temperature following ASTM E9, with a crosshead speed of 1 mm/min on cylindrical specimens of 8 mm diameter.
The lattice exhibited a yield strength of 245 MPa and an elastic modulus of 3.1 GPa, while the fully dense reference reached 960 MPa under the same test protocol.
Failure initiated by layer-by-layer collapse at the stress concentrators near the nodes, as confirmed by in-situ imaging at 30 frames per second.
Table 2. Mechanical properties: lattice, yield strength 245 MPa, modulus 3.1 GPa, densification strain 62 percent; dense reference, yield strength 960 MPa, modulus 110 GPa.
The authors attribute the lower yield strength of the lattice to nodal stress concentrations, but fatigue life was not measured in this study.
Post-processing by hot isostatic pressing at 920 degrees C and 100 MPa for 2 h increased the yield strength to 268 MPa, an improvement of about 9.4 percent.
